verdict.rationale: Lium documents Volumes as storage that outlives pods and can be attached to a pod, mounted at /mnt. That directly covers keeping datasets and checkpoints beyond a single GPU rental. Separately, local-volume backups every 6 hours with 2-day retention can be restored on another node. missing for 10: explicit confirmation that volumes are network-attached and reattachable across different nodes or regions, documented size and pricing limits, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can attach persistent network storage that survives instance teardown, so datasets and checkpoints outlive any single GPU rental

citations.quote: A **Volume** is storage that outlives your pods. Attach one to a pod and it is mounted at **`/mnt`**.
the pod's local volume is backed up every 6 hours and kept 2 days, so you can restore it on another node
